s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial papules with angiofibroma-like histology
salient_findings: Skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules over the chin, nose, and perinasal region
Papules increased in size and number since age 18
Dozens of papules present on physical examination
key_facts: 28-year-old white man
Papules first noticed at age 18
Right renal transplant at age 14
Dozens of skin-colored dome-shaped papules on face
No hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, or Shagreen plaques
Dental examination showed conical-shaped teeth
Biopsy of facial papule showed dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels
Electron micrograph showed dermal fibroblast with crystalline inclusions

shortlist.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
shortlist.why_kept: Angiofibroma-like histology and facial papules are characteristic of this disease

shortlist.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple facial fibrofolliculomas and renal issues are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Fibrofolliculoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic analysis showing angiofibroma-like features is compatible with this condition

shortlist.label: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Renal transplant history and potential endocrine abnormalities make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lipoid Proteinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Dermal fibroblast inclusions and skin-colored papules are consistent with this rare condition

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple angiofibromas, as indicated by the biopsy of facial papules showing dome-shaped lesions with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels, along with the history of renal transplant which could be related to renal angiomyolipomas, and the dental findings of conical-shaped teeth, are all consistent with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

rejected.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
rejected.why: Primarily associated with lung cysts, spontaneous pneumothorax, and renal tumors, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Fibrofolliculoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with solitary or a few lesions and is not associated with systemic manifestations like renal transplant

rejected.label: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1
rejected.why: Characterized by the occurrence of tumors in multiple endocrine glands, which is not indicated in the case

rejected.label: Lipoid Proteinosis
rejected.why: Characterized by the presence of hyaline deposits in the skin and other tissues, and typically involves the oral mucosa and other areas not primarily mentioned in the case
